am-hymenochirus-sp.title: African Dwarf Frog
am-hymenochirus-sp.summary: A small, fully aquatic frog from the rainforest pools and slow rivers of Central Africa. It breathes air at the surface, stays peaceful, and suits a calm, planted tank with gentle filtration. Trade animals are usually H. boettgeri; care is the same for all Hymenochirus.
rows: Up to about 3 in (7.5 cm); H. boettgeri females reach about 1.4 in (35 mm)
Long, shallow tank with a tight lid; 15 gal for a group of 3 (Aquariadise). Pete's Aquatics lists 10–20 gal
Peaceful; easily outcompeted for food, so avoid nippy or pushy tankmates (bettas are a poor match)
Social; keep at least 3 (Aquariadise) or a small group of 2–4 (Pete's Aquatics)
Carnivore: frozen or live bloodworms, mosquito larvae, brine shrimp and other worms, plus sinking prepared foods. Target-feed, and feed adults every other day so they do not get fat
Central and West Africa (H. boettgeri: Nigeria and Cameroon east to the DR Congo); still, shaded water in lowland rainforest and pools by slow rivers
notes: An aquatic frog, not a fish: it must reach the surface to breathe, so avoid very tall tanks and leave a gap under the lid.
Use sand rather than medium gravel, which can be swallowed. Floating plants give it places to rest near the surface.
Floating motionless at the surface ("burbling") is normal behavior. Do not handle it.
